questions.hint: Free software still has a bill: servers, upgrades and people on call.

options.label: Airbyte runs it for me
options.why: you want a hosted option with no servers to run

options.label: My team runs it on our own servers
options.why: Core is free software you deploy and upgrade yourself

questions.q: How much data will you sync each month?
questions.hint: Rough guide: 4 credits is about 1 GB of database data.

options.label: A few GB, under about 39 credits
options.why: below about 39 credits a month, Standard costs less

options.label: Tens to hundreds of GB
options.why: past about 39 credits, Plus costs less than Standard

options.label: Lots of data and many parallel syncs
options.why: Pro and Flex are priced by capacity, not by data volume

questions.q: How fresh does the data need to be?

options.label: Every 15 minutes
options.why: Plus lists 15-minute syncs, and Pro and Flex go faster

options.label: Every 5 minutes
options.why: Airbyte lists 5-minute syncs for Pro and Flex, and only hourly or 15-minute syncs for Standard and Plus

questions.q: Does your data have to stay inside your own network?

options.label: Yes, it must not leave
options.why: Enterprise Flex is hybrid and Core is self-hosted

options.label: No, a hosted service is fine
options.why: no network limit, so any hosted plan can work

questions.q: What kind of price do you need?
questions.hint: Pro and Enterprise Flex have no public price.

options.label: A published price I can check today
options.why: Pro and Enterprise Flex prices are not published

options.label: I can ask sales for a quote
options.why: you accept a quote for capacity plans

options.label: Free software, I will pay in staff time
options.why: Core software is free, but servers and people cost money

core.name: Airbyte Core
core.summary: Free, self-managed software you deploy yourself, usually with a Helm chart on Kubernetes.
core.bestWhen: your engineers want to run it, or your data must stay in your own network.
core.watchOut: you pay for servers, storage, upgrades, monitoring and on-call people, and Airbyte publishes no figure for that.

standard.name: Cloud Standard
standard.summary: Pay as you go: $20 a month with 5 credits, then $5 per extra credit.
standard.bestWhen: you are a small team with a few sources and under about 39 credits a month.
standard.watchOut: syncs are hourly, new subscribers get no SSO, and above about 39 credits Plus costs less.

plus.name: Cloud Plus
plus.summary: A tiered credit plan from $189 for 40 credits, with 15-minute syncs, SSO and two workspaces.
plus.bestWhen: you use more than about 39 credits a month and want a lower total than Standard.
plus.watchOut: each tier has a fixed credit count, and credits above it are billed as extra.

pro.name: Cloud Pro
pro.summary: A capacity plan sold in Data Workers, with syncs as often as every 5 minutes, SSO and RBAC.
pro.bestWhen: you run many parallel syncs and need strict governance.
pro.watchOut: the price is not published, and neither is the price of a Data Worker.

flex.name: Enterprise Flex
flex.summary: A capacity plan with hybrid deployment: Airbyte runs the control plane and the data stays in your boundary.
flex.bestWhen: you want a hosted control plane but your data must stay inside your own network.
flex.watchOut: the price is not published, so you must ask for a quote.
